items.title: Floods forecast in nine Kelantan districts until Wednesday
items.summary: "In Kota Baru, areas at risk are located within the Kelantan River Basin, while in Tumpat, they are within the Golok River Basin, covering Sungai Golok, Sungai Pengkalan Nangka, Sungai Mentua and Sungai Kelaboran," it said in a statement. In Bachok, areas at risk are within the Kemasin River Basin, including Sungai Jelawat, Sungai Kemasin, Saliran PKS, Saliran KADA and Sungai Bator. The Semerak River Basin, covering Sungai Lubuk Nibong, Sungai Melor, Sungai Gunong and Sungai Semerak, is also at risk of flooding.

items.title: NST Leader: Don't let Malaysia's connectivity be a gateway for drugs
items.summary: SITTING astride the Strait of Malacca in the centre of Southeast Asia has brought the country immense blessings, from being a shipping hub since time immemorial to being an essential aviation centre for regional and international airlines in more recent times. With this has come trade and tourism, making Malaysia a strategic magnet for people from all over. The same connectivity that makes the country a regional trade, aviation and logistics hub also provides opportunities for drug traffickers to move their illicit cargo across borders.

items.title: Floods forecast in Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin until Wednesday
items.summary: In Kuantan, the areas at risk include locations within the Sungai Kuantan Basin, covering Sungai Kuantan, Sungai Lembing, Sungai Kenau, Sungai Beserah, Sungai Belat and Sungai Soi. Also at risk are areas within the Sungai Cherating Basin (Sungai Cherating), Sungai Pahang Basin (Sungai Lepar) and Sungai Penor Basin (Sungai Penor). In Pekan, the affected areas are within the Sungai Bebar Basin (Sungai Bebar), Sungai Miang Basin (Sungai Miang), Sungai Pahang Basin (Sungai Pahang, Sungai Pahang Tua and Sungai Mentiga) and Sungai Mercung Basin (Sungai Mercung).

items.title: Binance's US$6.3b heist set to trigger tougher insurer scrutiny
items.summary: LAST week's US$6.3 billion Binance heist is prompting insurers to scrutinise cryptocurrency companies' security more closely, with underwriters expected to probe if clients are vulnerable to a similar attack when they seek new coverage or renew existing policies, industry insiders and experts said. The attack underscores the limits of the insurance coverage available for the fast-growing over US$2.5 trillion industry. No available crypto insurance could cover a loss of the scale suffered by Binance, experts said, while many policies have exclusions for state-backed cyberattacks.

items.title: Bersekutu Bersatu backs proposed appointment of Gerakan member in state assembly
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU: Terengganu's Bersekutu Bersatu wing has no objection to the state government's proposal to appoint a Gerakan member as an appointed assemblyman. State Bersekutu Bersatu wing chief Lim Chew Sieng said the proposal to appoint an assemblyman to look after the welfare and interests of non-Muslim communities was raised by the wing two years ago. He said the state wing welcomed Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar's proposal to appoint a representative from a party within the Perikatan Nasional coalition.

items.title: Tensions resurface between Prabowo and predecessor Jokowi
items.summary: Prabowo, a former general with a checkered past, shares a long and complex history with Joko Widodo, the former president better known as Jokowi. Jokowi defeated Prabowo twice in the 2014 and 2019 presidential elections. Jokowi has rejected those allegations.

items.title: Terengganu to name Gerakan member as appointed assemblyman
items.summary: MELAKA: The Terengganu government will appoint a Chinese member of Gerakan as a state assemblyman to represent the community, which currently has no representation in the state assembly. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar said the proposal had been studied for several months and approved by the Terengganu State Executive Council. "I want to announce today that we have agreed to appoint one state assemblyman from the Chinese community because the Terengganu State Constitution has a provision to appoint any race or gender that has no representation," he said.

items.title: Poland says Austrian woman among killed in Krakow shooting
items.summary: KRAKOW: A Polish regional official said on Sunday that an Austrian woman was among the six people killed in a shooting in Krakow after a man opened fire at random in the historic city centre. "I can confirm that the 51-year-old woman, who is the sixth victim of this attack, is an Austrian national," Malopolska region Governor Krzysztof Kleczar told reporters. The four others killed were Polish.

items.title: Eisenkot given tough task of forming Israeli government to replace Netanyahu
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Israel's former military chief Gadi Eisenkot was set on Sunday to be given the tough task of forming a government, with weeks to cobble together a coalition to replace Benjamin Netanyahu, the country's longest-serving prime minister. Eisenkot, 66, a political novice who has vowed to bridge Israel's deep polarisation under Netanyahu, was due to meet President Isaac Herzog, who will formally give him the mandate to form a government, with an initial deadline of 28 days. In consultations with Herzog last week, Eisenkot received recommendations from parties accounting for 67 lawmakers, against 46 for Netanyahu.

items.title: Four firearms seized at Krakow shooting scene, seven at gunman's home
items.summary: MOSCOW: Four firearms were seized at the scene of a shooting in the Polish city of Krakow, while another seven were found at the gunman's home, Kielce District Prosecutor Daniel Prokopowicz said on Sunday, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti. "Seven firearms and a large quantity of ammunition were seized at the shooter's residence. Four weapons were recovered at the crime scene in Krakow," Prokopowicz told reporters.

items.title: Deepavali cheer across borders
items.summary: LETTER: This is my third year not being able to celebrate Deepavali at home, in a part of the United Kingdom where the festival is not even routinely known or recognised. Their Deepavali advertisement from 2003. It was quite a sensation back then, and remains one of their most memorable.

items.title: Couple posing as police personnel caught by villagers in Dungun
items.summary: DUNGUN: A husband and wife who posed as police personnel to extort an elderly woman were cornered and caught by villagers at Felda Rasau Kerteh 3 around 4pm today. The incident began when the victim, Mariani Ismail, 64, received a video call from one of the suspects, who was dressed in a police uniform against a background resembling the Kuantan district police headquarters. Mariani's husband, Zakaria Ibrahim, said the suspects initially acted cautiously and refused to enter the house.

items.title: Malaysian suspect arrested with 102kg syabu in Brunei was en route to Sabah
items.summary: Federal Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the 46-year-old suspect was from Miri, Sarawak, and had two previous criminal records. "Police received information from Brunei's Narcotics Control Bureau (NCB) regarding the arrest of a Malaysian man by Brunei Customs at the Sungai Tujoh Control Post. Hussein said information from the Brunei authorities indicated that the suspect was believed to have used the country as a transit route before re-entering Malaysia.

items.title: [UPDATED] Train collision in Egypt's Giza injures 120
items.summary: CAIRO: Two trains collided south of the Egyptian capital on Sunday, derailing several carriages and injuring at least 120 people, state newspaper Al-Akhbar Al-Youm reported. Egypt's railway authority said a train travelling from Giza to Fayoum crashed into the rear of another service heading south from Cairo to the city of Aswan. Emergency crews used cranes to remove the wreckage, the authority said.

items.title: Melaka Chetti community keeps Deepavali traditions alive
items.summary: MELAKA: Deepavali celebrations by the Melaka Chetti community at Kampung Chetti had a distinctively festive atmosphere, with the Festival of Lights marked by a spirit of goodwill, harmony and family togetherness. However, public understanding and knowledge of the unique culture and history of the Melaka Chetti community remain limited, particularly among those outside the community, leading to misconceptions about its true identity. Many people, especially those from outside Melaka, are unfamiliar with the community.

items.title: Man held over alleged rape of 14-year-old niece in Besut
items.summary: BESUT: Police have arrested a 40-year-old man to assist in investigations into the alleged rape of his 14-year-old niece. Besut police chief Superintendent Mohd Rozaime Ab Rahim said police received a report on the case today before arresting the local man at his home in Kampung Raja at 2.45pm. Rozaime said police viewed all forms of sexual crime involving children seriously.

items.title: Malaysia calls for stronger cybersecurity, child online safety
items.summary: He said Malaysia welcomed the draft Doha Ministerial Declaration, which outlined a comprehensive approach to addressing the opportunities and challenges of digital transformation. He said the declaration reflected three priorities central to Malaysia's national digital agenda, which were ensuring meaningful connectivity, promoting digital inclusion and fostering a safe and trusted digital environment. Fahmi said digital transformation must create opportunities for everyone regardless of geographical location or level of digital readiness.

items.title: Nine remanded over fatal brawl that killed teenager in Sibu
items.summary: SIBU: Nine suspects have been remanded for seven days until Nov 15 to assist in investigations into the stabbing of a 19-year-old man during a brawl yesterday. Sibu police chief assistant commissioner Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad said the suspects, aged between 16 and 42, were brought to court at 7.15am today for the remand application. All nine suspects were arrested at several locations around Sibu between 10am and 4pm yesterday.

items.title: 20-year-old man drowns while swimming at Taiping waterfall
items.summary: IPOH: A 20-year-old man drowned while swimming with four friends at Taman Suria Waterfall near Taiping this afternoon. Perak Fire and Rescue Department assistant director (Operations) Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said teams from the Taiping and Kamunting fire and rescue stations were dispatched to the scene after receiving a distress call at 2.10pm. Sabarodzi said firefighters performed cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) on the victim, but he was pronounced dead at the scene by Health Ministry personnel.

items.title: Two policemen hurt after patrol car overturns avoiding monkeys
items.summary: KUALA BERANG: Two policemen were injured when their patrol car skidded and overturned several times while trying to avoid a group of monkeys in the middle of the road at Kilometer 4 of Jalan Simpang Bukit Kepah–Tapah, Kampung Kepah, this evening. Hulu Terengganu police chief Superintendent Sharudin Abdul Wahab said police received information about the accident about 4.30pm. He said both officers from the Hulu Terengganu district police headquarters' Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Division were on patrol duty when the incident occurred.

items.title: Plane hits pickup truck during emergency landing in Florida
items.summary: MOSCOW: A small Cessna 172D Skyhawk aircraft crashed into a moving pickup truck while attempting an emergency landing in Florida, US, Lee County Sheriff Carmine Marceno said, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti. "The pilots attempted an emergency landing. During the landing, the aircraft crashed into the rear of a pickup truck," Marceno wrote on the social media platform X on Saturday.

items.title: Man dies after falling from 23rd floor of Bayan Lepas hotel
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: A 25-year-old man died after falling from the 23rd floor of a hotel in Bayan Lepas. Northeast acting police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said police were alerted to the incident at 7.13am following a report from the public. Abdul Rozak said crime scene and forensic examinations found no signs of foul play.

items.title: Isa Isarb: 'We were detained over spy suspicions during Indonesia haze shoot'
items.summary: In a statement posted on social media, Isa Isarb, whose real name is Isa Batharul Zaman, 28, said authorities also suspected them of receiving funds from certain parties to topple a government. He said their actual purpose in visiting Indonesia was to film a documentary on the haze. One of them asked whether I was Isa Batharul, although I am better known as Isa Isarb," he said.

items.title: BN-Perikatan cooperation may not translate into full voter support, says Melaka Pakatan chairman
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 8 — Cooperation between Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN) in the 16th Melaka state election does not guarantee a full transfer of votes between their supporters, despite the apparent advantage of such an arrangement on paper. State Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Adly Zahari said supporters of the two coalitions might not necessarily embrace the cooperation, while new voters could also influence the election outcome. For example, based on the Negeri Sembilan state election results, the highest vote transfer rate recorded was 70 per cent.

items.title: Krakow gunman's parents and sister found dead at family home
items.summary: WARSAW: The three people found dead at the home of the gunman who opened fire in Krakow's main square on Saturday were his parents and sister, Polish radio station RMF FM reported on Sunday, citing police. The station quoted police spokesman Andrzej Fijolek, according to German Press Agency (dpa). The man drove his car into Krakow's busy market square on Saturday and opened fire indiscriminately at passers-by.

items.title: Penang police address claims girl was returned to alleged abuser's home
items.summary: BALIK PULAU: Penang police have clarified details of a child sexual assault case involving an 11-year-old girl after an assemblyman raised concerns over her welfare and protection. Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim said the Southwest district police headquarters' Criminal Investigation Division received a report from a school principal at 11.15am on Oct 16, 2025. Acting on the report, police arrested the girl's father about 5.30pm the same day.

items.title: Police secure remand of nine suspects over deadly Sibu brawl
items.summary: SIBU, Nov 8 — Nine suspects have been remanded for seven days until Nov 15 to assist in the investigation into the death of a 19-year-old male believed to have been stabbed during a brawl here yesterday. Sibu District Police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad said the suspects, aged between 16 and 42, were brought to court at 7.15 am today for the remand application. He said a post-mortem examination completed today revealed that the victim died of chest injuries.

items.title: Heavy rain triggers flash floods in Taman Sri Muda, no displacement reported
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 8 — No evacuations have been carried out in Taman Sri Muda, Section 25 here following flash floods triggered by heavy rain this afternoon, which were also captured in videos circulating on social media. He said monitoring was also being carried out in other high-risk areas, including Jalan Kebun Bunga in Section 22, Section 13 and Jalan Kebun. Earlier, social media users shared updates on flash floods following heavy rain between 3 pm and 5 pm today.

items.title: Philippines rebukes officials over public comments about China
items.summary: MANILA: The Philippines' Foreign Ministry issued a rare rebuke to government officials and agencies on Sunday over public comments about China, stressing the need for a unified voice as the country prepares to host a key regional summit. The Philippines' uniformed services have been engaged in a long-running war of words with the Chinese government over the South China Sea, a busy waterway that Beijing claims almost entirely despite an international ruling that its position has no legal basis. Multiple senators also called last month for Beijing's ambassador to be declared persona non grata after he suggested China could "easily win" any confrontation with the Philippines.

items.title: Man arrested 12 hours after stealing RM500 from Rembau mosque
items.summary: REMBAU: A man was arrested about 12 hours after stealing RM500 from a mosque donation box in Kampung Seberang Batu Hampar, early today. Rembau police chief Superintendent Ngiam Ooi Ming said police received a report on the break-in at 9.03am. Acting on information, a team from the Rembau district police headquarters arrested a man around 2.20pm.

items.title: Drain overflow causes flash floods in Taman Sri Muda — Fire and Rescue Dept
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Overflowing drains caused flash floods in several areas around Section 25, Taman Sri Muda, Jalan Kebun, Kampung Baru Hicom in Section 26 and Section 13 here today. Heavy rain from 3.15pm caused water to accumulate in several flood-prone areas. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the Shah Alam Fire and Rescue Station reported that water levels were beginning to recede after the rain stopped.

items.title: 'Trump has cost us': After midterm losses, MAGA asks if it's over
items.summary: "People are pissed off at Trump. Trump has cost us," he said, capturing a sentiment rippling through the president's Make America Great Again movement after the Republican Party's worst electoral defeat in decades. Across the coalition, some supporters who once viewed Trump as MAGA's greatest asset are beginning to question whether he has become its biggest liability.

items.title: Second 5G network achieves 90pc coverage ahead of schedule, says Fahmi
items.summary: He said the achievement marked significant progress in Malaysia’s transition towards a dual 5G network model aimed at strengthening competition, encouraging investment and improving telecommunications service quality. Fahmi said Malaysia had also made significant investments in expanding and strengthening its digital infrastructure through the National Digital Network Plan (JENDELA) since 2020. Fahmi said Malaysia had also made substantial progress in 5G deployment, with the second network achieving 90 per cent coverage nine months ahead of schedule.

items.title: Malaysia to leverage AI and satellite networks for disaster preparedness
items.summary: DOHA, Nov 8 — Malaysia sees significant opportunities to leverage satellite connectivity and artificial intelligence (AI) to strengthen disaster preparedness and communications resilience, said Communications Minister Datuk Fahmi Fadzil. He said Malaysia also saw potential in integrating terrestrial and non-terrestrial networks to strengthen communications resilience during emergencies. Fahmi said Malaysia was placing greater emphasis on strengthening emergency telecommunications capabilities to ensure essential communications remained available when conventional networks were disrupted.

items.title: Nations must decide own digital future, not be dictated to, says Fahmi
items.summary: DOHA, Nov 8— Malaysia has called for greater respect for national sovereignty in shaping telecommunications policies, warning against a form of “technology colonialism” in which technologically advanced nations dictate how other countries develop and deploy their digital infrastructure. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said every nation must retain the freedom to determine its own technological direction, particularly as geopolitical rivalries and competing technology ecosystems increasingly influence global telecommunications development. Fahmi said Malaysia’s experience in rolling out its 5G network demonstrated the importance of maintaining policy independence while navigating complex geopolitical and diplomatic considerations.

items.title: Police raid unlicensed KL entertainment outlet, detain 195 underage patrons
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — Police detained 195 underage teenagers and a premises manager in a raid on an unlicensed entertainment outlet in the capital after midnight last night. Dang Wangi district police chief ACP Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said the teenagers detained in the operation, conducted at about 12.30 am, comprised 93 local males, 61 local females, 16 foreign males and 25 foreign females. He said 16 outlet workers and 219 other patrons were also checked.

items.title: Melaka polls: Pakatan candidate for Paya Rumput aims to ease voting process with personalised polling slips
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 8 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) candidate for the Paya Rumput state constituency Datuk Azman Abidin has introduced an initiative to help voters check their polling locations and channels ahead of the 16th Melaka State Election on November 14. Azman, popularly known as Tok Man, said he and his campaign team would assist voters in checking their polling details while campaigning, with the results printed on small slips and handed to them for reference. “Under this initiative, campaign workers only need to enter a voter’s identity card number to retrieve information on their polling location, including the school and assigned polling channel,” he told reporters after attending a courtesy visit and meet-and-greet programme with the Paya Rumput state constituency campaign machinery today.

items.title: Penang Sentral offers round-the-clock waiting space for travellers, says Zairil
items.summary: BUTTERWORTH, Nov 8 — Penang Sentral, an integrated transport hub and major commercial development, provides a 24-hour waiting area on Level 1 at its stage bus platform, equipped with basic facilities for passengers. Penang Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the facility was intended for passengers waiting for buses or their next connecting transport service. He said Penang Sentral was operated by Malaysian Resources Corporation Bhd (MRCB) and not the state government, adding that the waiting area was not meant to serve as accommodation or an overnight stay facility.

items.title: MetMalaysia warns of prolonged rain in four states until Wednesday
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of continuous rain at the alert level for several areas in Kelantan, Pahang, Sabah and Terengganu, until Wednesday. In a statement, MetMalaysia said the warning covers Tanah Merah, Pasir Mas, Tumpat, Kota Bharu, Machang, Bachok, Pasir Puteh, Kuala Krai and Jeli in Kelantan. In Pahang, the areas affected are Kuantan, Pekan and Rompin, while the warning covers the whole of Terengganu.

items.title: Melaka plans five-year push to transform Kota Laksamana into state capital
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 8 —Kota Laksamana has the potential to become the new state capital of Melaka due to rapid development that can catalyse economic growth and transform the state's landscape, says Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh. Ab Rauf said the development plan also encompasses areas under the Straits of Melaka Waterfront Economic Zone (SM-WEZ), covering commercial, residential, healthcare and tourism sectors. Commenting on preparations for the Northeast Monsoon, Ab Rauf said the state government has stepped up disaster preparedness, including identifying 102 flood hotspots across the state.

items.title: BN-Pakatan relationship unaffected by Najib pardon issue, says Zahid
items.summary: ISTANBUL, Nov 8 — Differences in political views and positions among parties in the Unity Government have not affected the smooth administration of the government, said Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. He said the working relationship between BN and Pakatan Harapan (PH) in the government remained good, with the administration of ministries and Cabinet meetings proceeding smoothly and professionally. Elaborating, the Deputy Prime Minister said differences in political approaches and positions among parties should be addressed maturely, particularly when political situations differ at the federal and state levels.

items.title: Flood-prone areas under close watch as wet weather looms in Penang
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Nov 8 — The Penang Fire and Rescue Department has stepped up patrols and monitoring in flash flood-prone areas throughout the state following forecasts of rain and thunderstorms until Tuesday. He said today’s forecast indicated rain in several areas in the morning, followed by thunderstorms in most areas in the afternoon and rain in most places at night. Mohamad Shoki said that on Tuesday, rain was forecast in several coastal areas in the morning, while conditions were expected to ease slightly in the afternoon and evening, although thunderstorms and rain were still forecast in some areas.

items.title: Was a BN convoy given priority? Two-car collision at Melaka traffic lights sparks questions
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 8 — A Threads video is raising questions over whether traffic police gave a Barisan Nasional (BN) convoy priority at the time of a two-car accident at a junction on the Alor Gajah-Melaka Tengah-Jasin (AMJ) highway. On social media, someone remarked that the convoy vehicles carried BN campaign stickers and asked what had earned the group priority on the road. It noted that the convoy vehicles carried BN campaign stickers, and asked what had earned the group priority on the road.

items.title: Perak MMEA seizes vessel, probes unauthorised anchoring and reporting lapses
items.summary: IPOH, Nov 8 —The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) in Perak detained a cargo vessel suspected of violating the Merchant Shipping Ordinance 1952, about 4.3 nautical miles southwest of Pulau Jarak, near Lumut, yesterday. Its director, Maritime Captain Zainudin Mohd Zuki, said the Lumut Maritime Surveillance System radar detected the Gambian-registered vessel, prompting the Perak Maritime Headquarters Operations Centre to alert enforcement teams for inspection. He said the vessel had 21 crew members, including 11 Pakistanis, eight Iranians and two Indonesians.

items.title: AKPS detains 28-tonne buffalo meat shipment over import document irregularities
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 8 — The Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) at Port Klang seized a consignment of buffalo meat, valued at RM413,728 and imported from India, at Port Klang on Friday (Nov 6). Port Klang AKPS commander Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal said an inspection conducted by enforcement officers at 10.40am detected discrepancies between the halal certificate documents submitted and the information declared in the import permit. Following this, the entire consignment weighing 27,984 kilogrammes (kg) was seized for further investigation,” he said in a statement posted on the Port Klang AKPS Facebook page today.

items.title: Fake cops cheat retiree of RM179,490 in money laundering scam
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 —A 73-year-old retiree lost RM179,490 after falling victim to a Macau scam involving fraudsters posing as police officers and accusing him of money laundering and drug trafficking. Brickfields police chief ACP Hoo Chang Hook said the victim was initially contacted by two unidentified individuals claiming to be police officers, who instructed him to surrender his bank cards, cash and jewellery for investigation purposes. Hoo said the victim lodged a police report after realising he had been cheated.

items.title: Melaka lacks a real capital, says Ab Rauf, who wants Kota Laksamana to be it
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 8 — Barisan Nasional (BN) wants to turn Kota Laksamana into Melaka’s state capital if it wins the seat in the coming state election, Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh said. “God willing, I am targeting Kota Laksamana to become the capital of Melaka,” he said at a campaign event at BN’s Kota Laksamana operations room here, attended by MCA president Datuk Seri Wee Ka Siong and BN candidate Melvin Chua Kew Wei. “So if we win Kota Laksamana, we will give the people of Kota Laksamana a centre that will become Melaka’s state capital,” he said.

items.title: MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm warning for 11 states, federal territories
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds are forecast to hit 11 states and all three Federal Territories until 6 pm today. In Kedah, the affected areas are Kulim, Bandar Baharu and Baling, while in Perak, the alert covers Bagan Datuk, Hilir Perak, Perak Tengah, Manjung, Kinta, Kampar, Kuala Kangsar, Larut Matang, Kerian, Selama, Batang Padang and Muallim. Meanwhile, in Sarawak, bad weather is forecast for Mukah (Dalat, Matu, Daro and Tanjung Manis), Sibu (Sibu), Bintulu (Tatau), Sri Aman (Pantu, Lingga and Sri Aman), Limbang, Miri (Marudi and Bario), Sarikei (Maradong), Kapit (Kapit) and Betong (Pusa and Betong).

items.title: Melaka first, Bersatu later: Perikatan chairman holds off on disciplinary action
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 8 — Perikatan Nasional (PN) is putting off any decision on whether to discipline Bersatu until the Melaka state election is out of the way. PN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar said the coalition had received complaints from its component parties about Bersatu’s conduct, Free Malaysia Today reported. PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan had earlier said the coalition would act against Bersatu for allegedly breaching its constitution, including by contesting against PN in the Negeri Sembilan polls.

items.title: MB: No dissolution of Negeri Sembilan assembly, Budget sitting to go ahead
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 8 — The Negeri Sembilan State Legislative Assembly will not be allowed to dissolve, and efforts will be made to ensure that its sitting takes place as scheduled, said Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim. There is no question of the state assembly being dissolved. He was responding to a question on the state government’s preparations for the upcoming state assembly sitting.

items.title: ‘Mandatory’: Khairy tells Umno and BN voters to back PAS in Bukit Katil
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 8 — Fewer than seven months after Umno formally welcomed him back, Khairy Jamaluddin is on the Melaka campaign trail telling Barisan Nasional (BN) supporters to vote for a PAS candidate. The former Umno Youth chief said BN voters in Bukit Katil must back the PAS candidate there under the electoral understanding between the two sides, the New Straits Times reported today. “Send word to our friends, for example in Bukit Katil, because there is a PAS candidate there and we did not field a BN candidate,” he was quoted saying at a campaign stop in Duyong.

items.title: Nearly 3,000 guests, one cake: Anwar joins MIC’s Deepavali celebration in Shah Alam
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 8 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today attended the Deepavali open house organised by MIC and the Maju Institute of Educational Development (MIED) at Mansion Oncidium Hall in Kota Kemuning here. Anwar spent time mingling with guests and dining with several political leaders, including former prime minister Datuk Seri Ismail Sabri Yaakob and MCA president Datuk Seri Dr Wee Ka Siong. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim (second from left) with MIC president and Maju Institute of Educational Development (MIED) chairman Tan Sri S.A. Vigneswaran (second from right) at the MIC and MIED Deepavali open house at Mansion Oncidium Hall in Kota Kemuning, Selangor on November 7, 2026.

items.title: Small Hindu communities, big Deepavali spirit in Sabah and Sarawak
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — Despite the relatively small Hindu population in Sabah and Sarawak, Deepavali celebrations today brought together people from diverse backgrounds, reflecting a strong spirit of unity. He said Deepavali celebrations typically began with an early-morning oil bath, followed by wearing new clothes and attending prayers at the temple around 8am. First-time visitor Geoffrey Lo, 50, said he was excited to experience the Deepavali celebrations at the temple.

items.title: Prayers, reunions and open houses: Malaysia welcomes Deepavali
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — A festive mood filled towns and cities across the country as Hindus ushered in Deepavali today with prayers, temple visits, family reunions and gatherings with friends and neighbours. At the Sri Subramaniar Swamy Temple in Batu Caves near here, the grounds were already buzzing with activity early this morning as families in colourful traditional attire arrived to offer prayers. In PERAK, about 10,000 Hindus gathered at the Kallumalai Arulmigu Subramaniar Temple at Gunung Cheroh in Ipoh from as early as 6.30 am to offer prayers.

items.title: Wheel off, bumper wrecked: Chery says collision, not faulty parts to blame for viral NKVE car damage
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — Chery Auto Malaysia has moved to head off online speculation after images of a damaged Chery Tiggo Cross with a detached wheel and its axle spread on social media. The incident happened when the Chery car collided with a Perodua Myvi on the New Klang Valley Expressway (NKVE) yesterday. The incident comes about a month after the Road Transport Department temporarily suspended the vehicle type approval certificate for the Chery Omoda 5 following a separate incident in Johor Bahru.

items.title: Heavy rain, strong winds expected in Johor, Melaka and parts of three other states
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — Several areas in five states are forecast to experience thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds until 3 pm today, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia). In Sabah, the affected areas are the West Coast and Interior, covering Keningau, Pensiangan, Tambunan and Sook; Kudat; Sandakan (Paitan, Labuk and Sugut, Sandakan, Tongod and Telupid); and Tawau (Kalabakan and Tawau). Similar weather conditions are also forecast in several areas in Pahang, namely Temerloh, Pulau Tioman, Bera and Rompin, as well as in Negeri Sembilan, covering Jempol, Tampin, Seremban, Rembau and Kuala Pilah districts.

items.title: Ceilings leak at Seberang Jaya Hospital, no patients affected (VIDEO)
items.summary: SEBERANG PERAI, Nov 8 — Healthcare workers were seen holding umbrellas indoors at Seberang Jaya Hospital last night as rainwater poured through leaking ceilings and spread across flooded corridors, in video footage that has since gone viral. Penang Health director Dr Zulhizzam Abdullah confirmed that heavy rain and strong winds sent water seeping into several parts of the hospital, the New Straits Times reported today. “Most affected areas involved the hospital’s older building blocks, though several newer buildings were also impacted,” he was quoted as saying.

items.title: Health Ministry investigating claims of illness after consuming Gardenia products
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 8 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is awaiting laboratory analysis results and will conduct follow-up inspections at the Gardenia Bakeries (KL) Sdn Bhd factory to verify compliance with the Food Act 1983 following complaints of alleged food poisoning involving the company’s products. In a statement today, MOH said preliminary investigations were underway into complaints circulating on social media and media reports of alleged food poisoning after consumption of Gardenia products, particularly Gardenia Original Classic White Bread and Twiggies Choc-A-Lot. “MOH has sought an explanation from Gardenia Bakeries (KL).

items.title: Melaka Polls: Adly calls for transparency on BN's manifesto promises
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 8 — Barisan Nasional (BN) must provide detailed evidence to support its claim that it had fulfilled 97 per cent of the promises in its manifesto for the 15th Melaka State Election in 2021, said Melaka Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Adly Zahari. Adly, who is defending the Bukit Katil seat in the 16th Melaka State Election, said transparency in presenting manifesto achievements was important to ensure that every commitment announced by the government could be assessed based on actual implementation outcomes, rather than merely percentage figures. He also said that based on a summary of the Auditor-General’s Report, the Melaka government suffered a deficit in 2024, with revenue of RM490 million against expenditure of RM519 million.
